counterfactual_missing_items: No histopathologic or surgical confirmation of appendicitis
No explicit mention of an appendicolith/fecalith on CT
Patient was afebrile and denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation
decisive_items: Ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis
abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant

Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant, causing partial luminal obliteration and edema on the anterolateral aspect of the cecum
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete: it carries the appendicitis identity and adds the complication 'plastron' explicitly stated on ultrasound. R5 is the same identity but lacks the complication in the label. R1 is a mechanical-obstruction alternative with no ultrasound support and no target sign or lead point. R4 is contradicted by denied GI symptoms and by migratory RLQ pain and imaging.

rejected.why: Gastroenteritis is contradicted by the patient's denial of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation; migratory RLQ pain and imaging favor appendicitis.

Intussusception is not supported by the explicit ultrasound interpretation of plastron appendicitis; the CT linear lesion and cecal edema are more consistent with appendicitis, and no target sign or lead point is described.
